Original Mixology diagram by Ryan Harris, inspired by Herberto Graça’s Explicit Architecture. Source baseline 0d5e64b0455f7a5c96d4afada64654a5fdbb9a2c. Linked panels open implementation evidence.
svg.text: Explicit Architecture, with a Go accent
A detailed map of Mixology: conceptual responsibility, supported dependencies, execution, and evidence.

a.text: Policies and schemas owned per context

svg.text: Circle = responsibility map, not a literal import graph. Public contracts remain coupled to their named owners.

a.text: WITHIN A REGULAR CONTEXT / OWNERSHIP AND VISIBILITY
surfaces → public facade → typed pipeline → internal/commands + internal/dao; queries and handlers may use their own DAO.
models / queries / events are public contracts. Tagging reacts through handlers and owns association writes in internal/dao.
Peer reads use supported query contracts. Commands publish only their own events. Handlers cannot import facades or commands.

svg.text: EXECUTION / ONE LOCAL TRANSACTION / NUMBERED DASHED ARROWS
Retirement: IngredientDeleted → Drinks / Inventory / Menus / Orders. Preparation is per event; HandlerContext cannot AddEvent.
Failure: owner rolls back, then records failed attempt. One command claims each transaction; nested and sequential command composition is rejected.

a.text: Kernel does not depend on domains.
Gets authorize results; lists elide denials.
Audit explains effects; it is not a replay log.

svg.text: Current scope: seven contexts and three UI runtimes. Procurement, Analytics, process managers, brokers, and outboxes are future design pressures.
Colored regions group responsibilities; linked panels provide the code trace.
Original diagram; progressive approach inspired by Herberto Graça’s Explicit Architecture. Open SVG directly to follow source links.
